news.title: Michaely Bihina: The Cameroon goalkeeper making waves at Wafcon 2026
news.lede: Michaely Bihina has kept three clean sheets in five matches at Wafcon 2026. One name has become the toast of Cameroon following her heroics at the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon). Some in the Central African nation are already calling for a statue to built in honour of Michaely Bihina after her incredible performances which have helped the Indomitable Lionesses return to the final for the first time since 2016. The young goalkeeper has been one of the stars of the tournament with player-of-the-match performances against Nigeria in the quarter-finals and hosts Morocco in the last four.

news.title: Call to increase funding for refugee football - and boost Scotland's World Cup hopes
news.lede: The Refugee World Cup Scotland which is staged at the Toryglen Regional Football Centre on the South Side of Glasgow every summer has grown hugely and diversified greatly during the 14 years it has been running. Just eight five-a-side teams took part when the tournament – which was set up by Abdul Bostani, the managing director of the charity Glasgow Afghan United, in 2012 - was first held. But back in June there were no fewer than 24 seven-a-side teams, four of which were comprised entirely of women for the first time ever, involved. In total, over 250 people from more than 50 different countries were in attendance.

news.title: Ghana clear major hurdle in bid to end 20-year World Cup absence
news.lede: Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens. Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens, showed great courage to come from behind and defeat Côte d'Ivoire 2-1 in Casablanca. This victory keeps their dream of playing in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup alive. The match started badly for Ghana.

news.title: NZ Football pulls support for Infantino as FIFA President
news.lede: New Zealand Football has pulled its support for Gianni Infantino as FIFA President amid the fallout from the embattled executive's failed World Cup sell-off plan. NZ Football, which governs the game in Aotearoa, also called for an independent review of the steps taken during the plan's development. "After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within FIFA have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust," it said in a statement. "NZF believes this point in time represents an opportunity for all FIFA member associations to advocate for stronger governance, accountability and transparency which are fundamental in maintaining confidence of the administration of the global game."

news.title: Ryanair brutally mocks Argentina after World Cup winner Rodri spotted on ultra-low-budget flight
news.lede: Ryanair has joined the growing social-media frenzy around Rodri's unlikely journey home, turning the Manchester City midfielder's viral economy-flight appearance into an opportunity for some football banter. After the Spain international was photographed boarding one of its flights from Madrid to Liverpool, the airline aimed its latest joke at Argentina with a pointed message about who qualifies as a “winner”. Football News: Ryanair joins the football banter after Rodri, the World Cup-winning midfielder, is spotted on a budget flight, provoking a cheeky response aimed at Argentina.

news.title: Africa’s Representatives Take Shape for 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil
news.lede: Rabat - Africa’s lineup for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup is taking shape, with four nations securing direct qualification for the tournament in Brazil. Morocco, Malawi, Cameroon, and Algeria earned their places after reaching the semifinals of the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON). While Morocco is hosting the continental tournament, its place at the 2027 World Cup was not automatic. The Atlas Lionesses secured qualification on the pitch by defeating defending champions South Africa 2–1 in the quarterfinals.
